hyphae

hyphae is a GPL-3.0-or-later, specification-derived IMS/VoLTE client for Linux phones. When 2G and 3G were switched off, Linux phones lost voice, because the AP-side IMS stack has never been open source. hyphae is the missing control plane: SIP, IMS-AKA, registration, dialogs, SDP, carrier profiles, the Gm security plane and a codec-agnostic media boundary.

It is a library and a lab client, not a shipping dialer. The protocol surface is implemented and tested on a host with no modem and no network; the modem byte I/O and the licensed speech codec are the two pieces that stay outside the core.

What it owns

LayerOwnerResponsibility
SIP messages and transactionssipRFC 3261 encoding, headers, client/server transactions
Subscriber key and USIMaka, usimMilenage, AUTN checks, TS 31.102 AUTHENTICATE
Control planeimsREGISTER/AKA, dialogs, MO/MT calls, SMS, hold/resume, E911 construction
Carrier datacarrierTOML profiles keyed by MCC/MNC
Media framingmediaRTP/RTCP, jitter buffer, packet-loss concealment
Payload formatscodec-amr, evsRFC 4867 and TS 26.445 packet layout only
Bearer and securitytransportmock, UDP/TCP, AT/QMI, MBIM, CCCI boundary, ESP/IPsec

No default crate starts a thread, opens a socket or links a codec, so the whole protocol surface builds and tests on a laptop.

Status

Every implemented behaviour names a normative clause and the executable test that proves it; the requirement matrix is the project's evidence.

AreaState
Registration, IMS-AKA, USIMimplemented
Originating and terminating calls, CANCEL, PRACK, BYEimplemented
Hold/resume, call waiting, re-INVITE and UPDATE renegotiationimplemented
Forked INVITE, OPTIONS keepaliveimplemented
SMS over IMS, both directionsimplemented
Gm IPsec: authenticated ESP, SA negotiation, Linux XFRMimplemented
RTP/RTCP, jitter buffer, PLCimplemented
AT/QMI, MBIM, CCCI transportsmodelled or boundary only
Emergency request constructionimplemented; never transmitted
Byte-level modem I/O, live emergency callingout of tree or regulated

The licensing seam

IMS voice uses AMR-WB and EVS, which are patent-encumbered. hyphae keeps the protocol work separate from the codecs:

  • the core is GPL-3.0-or-later and contains no AMR-WB or EVS implementation; codec ships the trait plus royalty-free Opus.
  • AMR-WB lives in a separate, feature-off, patent-noticed package; its Apache-2.0 implementation library does not grant AMR-WB patent rights.
  • retrofit mode runs the phone's own licensed codec; manufacture mode uses an ODM or licensed build. Vendor blobs are never redistributed.
  • no code, strings or constants were derived from decompiled vendor binaries.

Try it

The client builds and tests against host-only code:

cargo test --workspace
cargo run -p ims --example register_flow
cargo run -p ims --example call_flow
cd lab/pris && ./run.sh   # full REGISTER over real UDP against a P-CSCF stand-in

The lab uses public 3GPP test credentials only. Live emergency calling is deliberately not reachable: the client builds the request and refuses to transmit it over any real transport.

Where it fits

hyphae is a consumer of the rest of the stack, not a replacement for it: the modem supplies the IMS bearer, the network supplies the P-CSCF and S-CSCF, and the host supplies identity and policy. It belongs beside the other runtime components rather than inside provisioning or transport.

Source, matrix, architecture notes and the codec-licensing decision: github.com/ajmwagar/hyphae.
